name: Sweden

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 10587710 inhabitants, recorded as 10.588 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Swedish, in the transversal venues pass. Three units, two houses and one stage, against an opening estimate of 2.5 produced with no research. All three are in Stockholm, which is itself the finding. Dockteatern Tittut has held its own stage at Lundagatan 33 by Zinkensdamm since 1994. It was founded in 1977 by Ing-Mari Tirén and Eva Gumpert as the first theatre in the world made for children from the age of two, and it names Kulturrådet, Stockholms Stad and Region Stockholm as its supporters — state, city and region together, which is as clean as the backing test gets anywhere in this record. Pygméteatern has a fixed stage on Vegagatan by Odenplan, has worked in puppetry since Sten Wallin and Michael Koitzsch founded it in 1976, pioneered modern shadow theatre in Sweden and now works in a mixed form of puppets, shadow play and actors; it draws most of its money from touring and carries support from Kultur Stockholm and the county, its Kulturrådet grant having been withdrawn some years ago. That withdrawal is worth recording rather than hiding: the venue survives on the box office and the remaining municipal support is what counts it. The stage is Marionetteatern, founded in 1958 by Michael Meschke, which since 2003 has been part of Stockholms stadsteater and keeps its home stage in the Kulturhuset at Sergels torg while also playing Skärholmen, Vällingby and Parkteatern. A named puppetry unit inside a municipal theatre, which is a stage exactly as the ruling of 2026-07-27 defines it, and the clearest instance of the pattern the ruling was written to catch. One refusal decides the shape of the count and it is a real loss. Byteatern in Kalmar was founded in 1971 and began as a puppet theatre for children, sailing the Swedish coast in the ship Helene with a café, film, music and puppetry; it has been the Kalmar county theatre since 1992, is funded by Region Kalmar län and Kulturrådet, and plays in a newly built performance house on Barlastgatan. It is not counted because it no longer describes itself as a puppet theatre: its own words are that it shall be a theatre for the whole of Kalmar county, producing for children, young people and adults. A theatre that came out of puppetry is not a puppetry unit, which is the line Kolibri settled and the same reading that removed Sarajevo and Skopje earlier in this pass. Three, and all three in the capital. Sweden funds its regional theatres well and none of them is a puppet house; what puppetry holds outside Stockholm, it holds without a hall.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. Stockholm University of the Arts, the only public higher arts school in the field after the mergers of 2014 and 2020, offers two puppetry courses, Introduction to Puppet Theatre and Introduction to Puppet Play, both as standalone courses outside any degree, one run in cooperation with the Marionetteatern at Kulturhuset stadsteatern. A standalone course is not a specialised degree-granting higher education programme: the denominator is not satisfied. The previous 0.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range. Caveat: this rests on search summaries, hence estimate and an upper bound of 1.
